title: Hardened hearts; image of the Father; foot-washing begins (John 12:38–13:8)
english: they were obstinate they disobeyed. The Jews murdered the Lord through their own ill will, not so that they might fulfill the prophecies; for if it were so they would have been irreligious in that way.

[John 12:38] God did not harden them, but allowed them to do what they wished. And they had the hardening from unbelief. Yet it was impossible that God’s foreknowledge, which foresaw the unbelief, not come out—not as compelling. Those unable to believe do not have a nature opposing belief, but a bad choice. Therefore the devil darkens them and God does not hinder.

[John 12:39] For this reason the prophets foretell, so that the sober may flee the devil’s pits; for “they could not” stands in place of “they would not”; and elsewhere too we understand power as choice.

[John 12:40] God did not harden their heart; for if he had, he would not have required of them an account, since he even forgives voluntary faults, but hands over the obstinate, blinded by the devil, to passions and a “depraved mind” (Romans 1:28); for while they were such, it was not just that they know the depth of the mystery—those who had shut the eyes of their mind.

[John 12:45] Being image of the Father he shows the Father through himself. Through this he signifies the indistinguishability of essence, showing the consubstantial; for the divine is incorporeal. These things signify likeness.
[John 12:45] Because of the hearers’ weakness he speaks as man. When I am honored, do not think you honor a man; for through me the Father is honored.

[John 12:46] As the Father is light, so also the Son. Therefore Paul, wanting to show the great resemblance, calls the Son “radiance” of the Father (Hebrews 1:3): just as light appearing makes both itself clear and the things seen, so the Son, being light and having come, made both himself and the Father known to us.
The aim of the present coming was not to judge but to save the faithful. And so as not to give them occasion for unbelief, he refers the cause of unbelief toward him up to the Father.

[John 12:48] For the word of his humility condemns them. The Son himself is going to judge the disobedient, not the word; for he speaks enigmatically. On the day of judgment the word that called us to salvation punishes those who disobeyed.

[John 12:49] Being Word of the Father he himself interprets what is in the Father and makes it manifest. Therefore he also says he has received a commandment; for so among us too word publishes what is in the mind.
[John 12:49] He says he does these things as from the Father, since the Jews saw him reshaping the shadow of the law toward the more spiritual.
[John 12:50] Saying this he did not abolish his own authority, but shows that nothing alien to the Father is in the Son. I utter nothing contrary to the Father, nor as mine alone, but as common.

[John 13:1] He foreknew the passion; therefore it must be said that he came willingly to suffer; for he would not unwillingly have endured so insulting a death. He calls hour the Passover feast at which he suffered; he calls his death a passing.

[John 13:1] He loved them even before the Passover, having become man; but when he also handed himself over to die, then he perfectly showed his love toward human beings. Not only Jews but also others he has as his own as Creator. He calls his own all who are in the world.
[John 13:2] He calls tradition the salvation of the faithful, which he himself also hands over in turn to the Father, because he was begotten from the Father’s essence.

[John 13:2] As astonished the evangelist says that he washed the feet of the one who had set himself to hand him over to death. On the fifth day the supper; on the fourth Judas agreed to betray Christ; therefore he said the devil had already cast into the heart that Judas should betray him.
[John 13:6] Through the touch he was cleansing their feet for readiness of the gospel. And he also leads them into humility.
[John 13:7] When I am taken up, he says, then from the Spirit’s grace you will learn what is happening.
[John 13:8] If you do not accept the lesson of humility, you have no share with me—that is, unless someone washes off the filth of sin through Christ’s grace, he does not

title: Peter, Judas, and mutual glory (John 13:8–33)
english: attain life nor enjoy the kingdom of the heavens.
[John 13:9] Having at first spoken against it through humility, now through excess of reverence Peter says something superfluous—both from fierce love.

[John 13:11] They were clean, enlightened by the teaching and freed from Jewish error and having cast off all wickedness by being with Christ. And by witnessing purity to the others he proves unclean the one who is not clean.
[John 13:13] By saying “I am” he showed that he is God by nature and teacher.
[John 13:14] Not because they were filthy did he wash them, but to teach them to be moderate. The basin does not hold the rank of a bath nor lighten sins, but leads toward perfect virtue.
[John 13:15] Not only in word but also in deed he gave the example of perfect humility.

[John 13:17] It is not knowing virtue that is to be emulated, but working it; for knowing and not doing brings greater punishment. Knowing happens to belong to many; doing does not belong to all. Therefore he said: blessed are you if you do them.

[John 13:18] Judas was not compelled to betray so that the Spirit’s words might come out—which is full of every blasphemy—but so that we may know that Scripture spoke about that one whom we see having done what was foretold. And if the Lord chose Judas and he transgressed, nothing follows from this; for he chose him while he was good, and he was changed like Adam and Saul; for God does not abolish free will, but allows each to act as he wishes, so that the wicked may be punished and the virtuous crowned.
[John 13:26] Through the morsel the Lord fulfilled the prophecy that says: “He who eats my bread has lifted up his heel against me” (Psalm 41:9; John 13:18).

[John 13:27] On the fourth day Satan cast into Judas that he should betray the Lord, and he spoke this to the Jews on the fifth toward evening. When he saw Judas wanting to betray the Lord in deed and hurrying to it, then he entered into him. So casting in is one thing and entering into him another, just as striking someone with the hand from outside is one thing and giving him an opening and thrusting the sword in is another.

[John 13:27] The evangelist calls the devil’s entrance the confirming of Judas to do what is pleasing to the devil. When God made him plain and set him apart, then the devil sprang upon him because of his measureless shamelessness.

He does not say this as commanding, but as reproaching the one he let do what he wished, since he did not want to be corrected. Since this is settled for you, hasten to the plot against me; for suffering does not grieve me.

[John 13:27] The morsel given him in the order of a blessing was not the cause of Judas’s apostasy, but the unchangeable wickedness after the exposure. Therefore the enemy also sprang in as into an ungated city.

[John 13:28] Since perhaps John said it to him secretly and he heard, no one knew; for if they had known, perhaps they would even have killed him—or because they were in turmoil, not knowing what was in Judas’s heart, they did not understand what was said.

[John 13:29] If someone says how the one fed from others’ means, who did not allow the disciples to carry a bag or purse, had a money-box, it must be said that this happened only for the sake of the poor.
[John 13:31] Even if the Son does all things, yet through what he does he ascribes them to the Father and glorifies the Father.
[John 13:31] Christ, as having put death to death through his own death, was glorified; he teaches that enduring what is shameful for God’s sake is glory.
[John 13:31] The Father was glorified in the Son, since it became known whose Father he is. So also the Son is glorified as having such a begetter.

[John 13:32] Through himself the Father will glorify the Son, and at once—that is, on the cross, when the sun was darkened, the rocks were split, and after fifty days the Spirit descending made the Son plain to all.
[John 13:33] They were seeking him as one who loves and as a teacher.
[John 13:33] He said this to human beings because of their unbelief; for with the disciples he was and is always present, and because after the resurrection they also

title: New commandment; Peter’s denial; way, truth, life (John 13:33–14:11)
english: saw him and ate with him.

[John 13:34] New is the form of this commandment, and beyond the law is loving the neighbor more than oneself. I do not want you to love those to whom you owe, but those to whom you do not owe; for I too die for you, to whom I owe nothing.
Not from the signs you do will you be known as my disciples—for that belongs wholly to grace from above—but from loving one another and having concord and giving yourselves.
[John 13:35] Christ is a son of love, who is love according to nature, being love itself by nature and fruit of love, not having the good of love as something acquired.

[John 13:36] Because of weakness he forbids Peter to follow him, yet later promises because of boldness. Since he too was going to be crucified as Christ was, he foretells what will happen to him alone.
[John 13:37] Peter has become a type for us of asking teachers what we do not know.
[John 13:37] Disbelieving somewhat what was said, Peter inquires, and so also promises to die for him.

[John 13:38] Since you do not want to be persuaded that what I say cannot fail to happen, you will know it in the denial. And he underwent this not because Christ led him into it, but because he left him bare, so that he might not be lifted into arrogance.

[John 13:38] Let no one say that Peter denied because Christ said so; for he did not lay necessity on him so that he should come to denial, but as God he foretells to the disciple what was altogether going to be. And the denial did not come from an unbelieving soul, but from weakness.
[John 13:38] Not all of you are going to deny, he says; Peter’s denial will be wiped out through repentance and confession.
[John 14:2] If the place in which you are going to be with me had not long ago been prepared for you, I would have gone away and prepared a place for you.

[John 14:3] There is no need to ascend for the sake of preparing a place for you, but so that I may make you a pasture of ascent where the angels’ dwelling is, which was impassable to all flesh. When therefore I do this, coming “in the regeneration” (Matthew 19:28) I take you with myself, that you may be where I am.

[John 14:6] He is way because through him they were coming and he himself was Lord of leading up to the Father. Truth because of truthfulness, that these things will altogether be. And life, because not even death itself, he says, will be able to hinder you from coming.
[John 14:6] He is way through the practical, truth as true definition of the faith, life as raising us and leading into incorruption and freeing from the ancient curse.

[John 14:7] Here he calls sight the knowledge according to mind. Therefore the one who contemplates the Son not in bare essence but clothed in flesh knows his equal Father in all things. Knowledge shows contemplation through notions; vision shows assurance through God-befitting works.
[John 14:8] As knowing the Son exactly he said this, thinking perhaps he could see God with the eyes.

[John 14:9] Nothing else, he says, is the Son except what the Father is while remaining Son; for even if you happen to say, Philip, that I know you, that you are Son, yet you have not recognized me, that having the whole Father in myself I remain again being Son.
[John 14:9] From what the Son has done both before incarnation and after incarnation, his infinite strength appears to the mind as “in a mirror” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

[John 14:9] The wording signifies the extreme resemblance and equality. Therefore, lest someone fall into Sabellius’s heresy by dividing the hypostases, he adds saying: the one who has seen me has seen the Father. And this he makes clear through knowledge. He says these things about the invisible essence of himself and of the Father; for it is not possible to see the divine with fleshly eyes. Therefore he said: the one who has seen me has seen the Father—not that he himself is the Father, but that through the extreme resemblance the one who sees the Son sees the Father; for each is self-subsistent.
